title: Adaptive Prefetch Bridge for Embeddings + Rerank SDKs — streaming ergonomics & cross-language examples
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a lightweight, language-agnostic 'adaptive prefetch bridge' that standardizes pagination/batching/streaming ergonomics for embeddings and rerank endpoints across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Goals: enable predictable latencies for mixed-size requests, provide cancellable streaming iterators/generators, surface retry semantics consistently across SDKs, and ship clear cross-lang examples and tests. Deliverables: (1) a small runtime shim in each SDK that implements sliding-window prefetch + backpressure, (2) documented retry profiles tuned for embeddings and rerank (idempotency semantics), (3) idiomatic streaming APIs (async generators for Python/TS, channel-based iterator for Go), (4) sample apps and benchmarks demonstrating parity and cost/latency trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Python/TS/Go SDKs expose a consistent high-level helper (named 'AdaptivePrefetch') that supports: page_size, max_inflight_requests, max_tokens_per_batch, and cancel() API; 2) Examples for embeddings+rerank show end-to-end code for batched embed -> rerank flow with <=10% median latency regression vs direct calls for small requests; 3) Integration tests that simulate flaky network and assert retries keep correctness and do not double-count tokens; 4) Documentation pages with sample snippets and a 'migration' note for existing iterator helpers; 5) Perf numbers included in PR description and Console dashboard link.

notes: Trade-offs considered: (A) exposing fine-grained batching knobs increases power but confuses users; we leaned toward opinionated defaults. (B) Retry semantics: embeddings are idempotent; rerank scoring requests may not be pure-read in future (if scoring hooks added) — implemented idempotency keys to be safe. (C) Memory vs latency: default conservative max_inflight_requests=3 to bound memory footprint for clients on low-memory devices.
